transcription.notes: Single task with three answer tables (Table I, II, III) transcribed as parts; the printed tables have no header row, so the first printed row serves as the Markdown header row. Four full sky charts (pages 3–6) are cropped as figures of the task. No points or time limit are printed. Printed name spellings are kept verbatim as names: Camelopardus, Eridano, Sagitarius, Procion, Alnilan, Menkaliman, Dumbell. The word 'algarisms' is kept as printed (intended word uncertain), and so is the printed agreement error 'This exam consist'. In the printed Table II the second column of row 3 and the fourth column of the last row are empty. The printed '( )Microscopium' lacks a space and is kept. Every page carries the IOAA 2012 masthead and a 'Student ID:' line, which are not transcribed.

problems.title: OBSERVATIONAL ROUND – 3RD NIGHT
problems.statement: This exam consist of 3 tables and 4 full sky charts in Equatorial coordinates, showing the sky for the four seasons. On those charts different objects are marked in different colours: constellations are noted in blue capital letters; stars are noted in red arabic algarisms and deep sky objects are noted in green small caps. The charts contain 20 stars, 20 constellations and 10 deep sky objects to be marked on tables I, II and III. Your task is to correctly address the objects in the tables.

figures.caption: Chart 1
figures.alt: Full sky chart 1 in a dashed circle with N at the top, S at the bottom, E on the left and W on the right, and the number 1 at the upper right. Constellation stick figures; blue letters A, B, C, D, F mark constellations, red numbers 1, 2, 3, 4 mark stars, and green circles a, c mark deep sky objects.
